limitations: The audit was read-only and did not execute a fresh install, pytest, Ruff, provider call, Runtime, or socket; retained captures and artifacts were replayed from bundle bytes.
The original candidate.2 tar.gz was not present; its materialized members, control files, receipt, and replay report were checked without seeking the external protected archive.
The upstream BFCL tracked-tree contents were not materialized; replay was limited to the sanitized tracked-name/status captures and bound per-path digests.
The six-row live stage-ledger JSONL was absent; only a checkpoint containing the three current rows was available.

findings.rationale: BootstrapModelExecutor accepts caller-selected ledger_path and failure_latch_path values. AttemptLedger exclusivity and slot-consumption checks apply only to that selected ledger. A caller can construct another executor with a different ledger and latch, replay the same authorization receipt, and receive a fresh copy of all 24 slot IDs. The test covers only one ledger/latch pair. The implementation therefore does not impose a candidate-global 24-call ceiling.
findings.required_action: Bind the authorization receipt to one fixed active ledger and latch, atomically acquire a candidate-global execution capability before any provider call, reject alternative paths, and add a negative test proving that two executor instances cannot consume the same slot or exceed 24 aggregate calls.
findings.title: Caller-selected ledgers permit repeated 24-slot bootstrap budgets

findings.rationale: build_quality_gate validates the AI approval and returns full_test_execution=AUTHORIZED_ONCE, but it never invokes consume_ai_test_access_capability. The atomic fixed-path consumption function is not called by any production full-test gate or runner in the materialized source. Re-running build_quality_gate with unchanged inputs reproduces authorization without recording use, so a one-use protected-test approval is reusable.
findings.required_action: Make the sole full-test execution boundary atomically call consume_ai_test_access_capability before accessing protected tests, bind the consumption receipt to the exact approval and inputs, reject every subsequent invocation, and add an integration test covering two attempted executions.
findings.title: The one-use full-test approval is validated but never consumed

findings.rationale: The closure builder runs pytest and Ruff from the repository root as pytest ... tests and ruff check scripts tests. The only intended DG-10 configuration is nested at evals/dg10/pyproject.toml, and no root pytest or Ruff configuration exists. Pytest and Ruff do not discover a child-directory configuration from those root invocations. Consequently the captures do not apply pytest strict-config/strict-markers or the declared Ruff E,F,I,B,UP,RUF,S selection, despite the report treating the nested configuration as part of the executed closure.
findings.required_action: Invoke pytest with an explicit configuration path and Ruff with an explicit --config path, record those commands and the configuration digest, then regenerate the fresh collection, pytest, Ruff, environment identity, worker-closure report, source inventory, and review bundle.
findings.title: R2 pytest and Ruff captures ignore the frozen DG-10 configuration

findings.rationale: The manifest correctly freezes 216 case IDs, category flags, languages, and the 80/122/24 denominators before any candidate.4 result access. It references candidate.4.5 worker closure fa4c57..., which is absent from current-source and the closed bundle. More importantly, the manifest contains no frozen adapter or attempt-ledger identity, while the scorer only requires worker_environment_sha256, adapter_sha256, and ledger_sha256 to be homogeneous across submitted rows. Caller-selected homogeneous identities can therefore define the execution provenance after result access.
findings.required_action: Issue a successor preregistration that materializes its referenced worker closure and freezes exact worker, adapter, ledger schema/root, and dependency identities before any result access; require every per-case receipt to equal those frozen identities.
findings.title: BFCL execution identities remain caller-selected after case preregistration

findings.rationale: The checkpoint declares six append-only entries and a prefix hash but materializes only current entries at sequences 2, 4, and 6. The referenced var/dg10/stage-ledger-candidate.4.2.jsonl is absent from the bundle. Although each included current row has a valid entry hash and the claim matrix agrees on REVIEW_REQUIRED, the missing rows prevent independent verification of global adjacency, the declared prefix digest, and the complete supersession history. The closed bundle therefore does not establish that one reconciled append-only ledger is the state source.
findings.required_action: Materialize the immutable six-row ledger JSONL in the review bundle, bind its size and SHA-256 in the manifest and checkpoint, and replay every global and per-stage link before regenerating the audit bundle.
findings.title: The stage checkpoint omits the append-only ledger needed for reconciliation

parent_finding_closures.rationale: Authorization now replays fixed candidate-bound artifacts and active identities; controlled decision and release entry points remain unconditionally fail-closed.

The importer requires the fixed active bundle and identities, recomputes every manifest/source entry and aggregate, validates the response schema, and binds two distinct successful xhigh event streams before it can emit receipts.
Only unanimous ACCEPT_R0_R2_FOR_T2_BOOTSTRAP outputs reach receipt creation; revised outputs cannot emit accepted stage receipts.
Claim validation fixes candidate.4, recomputes the canonical source root, resolves unique hashed gate receipts, and validates gate, stage, candidate, and evidence semantics.

The append-only ledger now validates immutable legal transitions, journals native acceptance and terminal events, classifies missing terminal evidence as unknown, and reconciles call slots rather than treating finalized attempts alone as complete.

The previously missing Runtime and runner bytes are materialized in one source identity; the content-addressed wheel, retained rebuild, fresh-install captures, and complete 356-entry runner closure replay exactly. The separate configuration-execution defect is reported as DG10-C4-AI-020.

Candidate.4 introduces a reachable post-R0-R2 AI receipt/import/authorization transition while retaining denial of test access and later model phases. The remaining aggregate slot-enforcement defect is tracked under DG10-C4-AI-015.

The quality gate now binds disjoint preregistered 50-case sets, both required strata, hard-safety/topology/ledger receipts, and a raw-event-verified two-thread AI approval. The distinct missing one-use consumption is DG10-C4-AI-019.

Exact cases and denominators are frozen, but adapter and ledger identities remain row-supplied homogeneous values and the manifest's candidate.4.5 worker-closure reference is absent from the closed source.

The serving gate has fixed active paths and rebuilds cells from hashed raw receipts plus the globally reconciled attempt ledger, enforcing workload/model bindings and global attempt/native-ID coverage; unset active hashes keep it fail-closed.
The audit schema truthfully represents AI_INDEPENDENT_PER_USER_POLICY, permits false protected-archive access, and does not claim human authority or release authority.

The source implements one ledger and the checkpoint states align, but the checkpoint omits rows 1, 3, and 5 and the referenced raw JSONL is not in the bundle, so its six-entry append-only history cannot be reconciled independently.

Authorization requires the fixed importer aggregate and active identity receipt, verifies their exact references, and replays both bound xhigh AI runs rather than accepting standalone caller-authored stage receipts.

A hand-authored approval no longer suffices: the validator replays a dedicated fixed-bundle importer, two distinct xhigh provider threads, raw events/output, active identity, policy, and exact input bindings.

Slots are preallocated and consumed before provider execution within one ledger, but caller-selected alternative ledgers and latches can each reuse all 24 authorization slots; the aggregate ceiling is not enforced.
runtime/migrations/script.py.mako is materialized and hash-bound in both the 383-entry source inventory and the regenerated 356-entry executed runner closure.
The successor acceptance contract and immutable amendment bind gpt-5.6-sol/xhigh, while the prior max process is explicitly interrupted and non-authoritative.

The independently rebuilt wheel is retained in the bundle, is byte-identical to the source wheel at SHA-256 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773, and its RECORD and Runtime source members replay exactly.

DG10-R0.rationale: The candidate.2 materialized 201-member replay, MANIFEST, SHA256SUMS, receipt, and immutable historical NO-GO are exact, and candidate succession is explicit. Nevertheless, the audit's global acceptance predicate forbids an ACCEPTED stage while a parent P1 and new P0/P1 findings remain open, and the complete stage-ledger chain is not materialized.

DG10-R1.rationale: Artifact-derived authorization, AI provenance, append-only attempt accounting, and release denial are materially improved. R1 remains open because the 24-call ceiling is resettable through alternate ledgers, the protected full-test approval is never atomically consumed at the execution boundary, BFCL execution identities remain unfrozen, and the stage-ledger chain cannot be replayed from the bundle.

DG10-R2.rationale: The content-addressed wheel, retained independent rebuild, fresh installation captures, 209-test collection/pass result, 356-entry executed-source closure, BFCL tracked-tree capture, and source/environment/model identities replay consistently. R2 is not semantically closed because pytest and Ruff were invoked from the root without the nested frozen configuration, so the claimed executed source/config closure and Ruff policy were not actually exercised.
